description: The item contract for the shared OBSERVATORY_METRICS DynamoDB table, provisioned by
the tarun-teamweave-shared stack and written by every weave service that emits span
telemetry. The table has many writers in different languages and several readers that
build dashboards from it, none of which can see each other's code, so the item shape
is a cross-repository interface and is pinned here rather than in any one consumer.
Copies vendored into consumer repositories must carry the same version string; a
conformance test in each repository asserts its writer or reader against this file.
v2.0.0 moves reads off the partition key. Under v1 a reader queried whole partitions
by exact pk, so a writer's rows were visible only if it had guessed the same pk prefix
grammar the reader enumerated -- and three of the five writers had not, leaving their
telemetry durable, billable and permanently invisible. Reads now go through the
SpanTimelineIndex GSI, which is keyed on a date bucket and a timestamp, so a reader
never needs to know what prefix a writer chose. The base-table pk is now a writer's
own business; the two index attributes are what every writer must get right.

note: DynamoDB attribute names are case sensitive and the table declares these exactly.
An item whose key attributes are spelled any other way (PK/SK, Pk/Sk) is rejected
by PutItem with a ValidationException, which a writer that swallows exceptions
will report as success while writing nothing at all.

sk_grammar.rationale: Readers range-query on sk lexicographically, so the timestamp must sort first and must be UTC ISO 8601.

note: The namespace is what makes a row findable. A reader queries whole partitions by
exact pk, so a writer using a namespace no reader enumerates is writing rows that
are durable, billable and permanently invisible to every dashboard.
This is the namespace the shared library exporter writes. No reader queries it.
Migrating a service off its vendored copy onto the library exporter (the stated
point of platform edge E2) therefore removes that service from every dashboard
without any error surfacing. Resolving this is a platform decision recorded in
docs/integration-audit.md, not something a consumer repository can fix alone.

required_attributes.span_date: S -- YYYY-MM-DD in UTC, the SpanTimelineIndex partition; normally timestamp[:10]
required_attributes.timestamp: S -- ISO 8601 in UTC, the SpanTimelineIndex sort key
required_attributes.operation: S -- what kind of call this span was; readers filter and group on it

recommended_attributes.service: S -- the emitting service; the only attribute that identifies a row's origin once several writers share the index

invariants: I1: key attributes are spelled 'pk' and 'sk' in lower case
I2: pk matches {namespace}#{discriminator} with a namespace listed in namespace_registry
I4: ttl is present and is a Unix epoch in the future, so rows expire rather than accumulate
I5: superseded in v2 -- reachability is no longer a property of the namespace, because reads go through SpanTimelineIndex rather than the partition key
I6: span_date is present and is YYYY-MM-DD, or the row is absent from every dashboard
I7: timestamp is present and is ISO 8601 in UTC, and agrees with span_date
I8: operation is present and non-empty

gsi.name: SpanTimelineIndex
why: Both readers already query one partition over a time range and then filter and
aggregate in memory. A date bucket plus a timestamp serves that directly while
requiring no agreement about vocabulary: keying the index on 'operation' instead
would have traded a pk-prefix convention for an operation-name convention, and a
reader wanting everything would still have had to enumerate the values.
caveats: A GSI indexes only items that carry BOTH key attributes. A writer that omits
span_date or timestamp is exactly as invisible as it was under v1, which is why
those attributes are required rather than recommended, and why I6-I8 exist.
The index is not retroactive: rows written before this contract have no span_date
and will not appear. They remain reachable by their original pk. Backfilling them
is a separate migration and is not attempted by the conformance tests.
span_date has one partition per day, so the current day is a write hotspot. At this
portfolio's volume that is well inside what on-demand adaptive capacity absorbs; if
write rates grow, bucket by hour (YYYY-MM-DDTHH) rather than reintroducing a
AWS creates at most one GSI per UpdateTable operation, so this must be deployed as
its own CloudFormation change, and its backfill must finish before readers switch.

namespace_registry_note: Kept for archaeology and for reading rows written before v2. Under v2 a namespace
carrying no reader is no longer a defect, because readers do not query by pk at all.
readers_for() is retained for the same reason and now answers a historical question.
